response.sql: SELECT P.SEX, AVG(L.DNA) AS avg_dna, AVG(L.ALB - L.TP) AS avg_alb_minus_tp FROM Laboratory AS L INNER JOIN Patient AS P ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE L.`T-CHO` >= 180 GROUP BY P.SEX

assumptions.assumption: The request doesn't say which side of the 180 cutoff to keep. The query keeps records with T-CHO >= 180, which means 180 or higher.
Rows with a NULL T-CHO are dropped by the filter. A NULL SEX, if any exist, forms its own group, and a blank-string SEX forms a separate group.
The average of ALB - TP only uses rows where both ALB and TP are present. It is left NULL if a group has no such rows, and it is not rounded.

alternatives.interpretation: Keep only records with T-CHO strictly below 180.

alternatives.interpretation: Keep only records with T-CHO strictly above 180, so a value of exactly 180 is excluded.
